title: Adaptive slab rebalancer + kvcache sweep to address intermittent GPU OOMs during hosted bursts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers across Hosted and Dedicated experienced intermittent GPU OOMs during short high-concurrency bursts. Metrics showed sustained per-GPU memory growth despite steady request sizes; heap fragmentation plus orphaned KV entries in the KV cache were observed. This ticket tracks the investigation, runtime patch (adaptive slab rebalancer + kvcache sweep), validation, and staged rollout to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private installs.
timeline: 2026-02-22: First customer report (enterprise A) of sudden 503s and worker restarts during nightly import job; on-call created Sev2 escalation.
2026-02-23: Observability correlates OOMs with 95th percentile request bursts; KV cache miss/hit ratios drifted upward and slab free lists showed fragmentation on affected nodes.
2026-02-24: Reproduced memory growth in internal load test by replaying customer traffic shape; heap compaction did not fully reclaim fragmented arenas.

2026-02-25: Hypothesis formed: small persistent KV tombstones + uneven slab allocation across arenas leads to low-utilization slabs that prevent reuse, causing effective memory pressure and infrequent OOMs.
2026-02-26: Implemented diagnostic build with additional KV index checks and slab allocation histograms; short canary in staging confirmed same pattern.
2026-02-28: Created this ticket and assigned owner; began design for mitigation that includes an adaptive slab rebalancer and kvcache sweep pass.
2026-03-04: Dev PR opened implementing compact-on-idle trigger and light-weight KV sweep (gh: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6421).
2026-03-06: Integration tests show reproducible reduction in peak resident set during burst windows (~22% lower on synthetic repro).
2026-03-08: Internal review found race on async KV tombstone cleanup; addressed with per-shard fencing and unit tests.
2026-03-09: Staged rollout to non-prod dedicated clusters; no regressions observed; latency unchanged within SLOs.
2026-03-10: Seeking approval for broader canary in Hosted with 1% traffic and Dedicated pilot; this PR is now In Review.
root_cause_summary: A combination of KV cache tombstone accumulation and slab allocator fragmentation prevented memory reuse under bursty allocation patterns. The allocator's free lists remained imbalanced across arenas, and periodic scans that used to reconcile tombstones were too infrequent for the workload shapes seen in Hosted burst traffic.
fix_summary: Introduce an adaptive slab rebalancer that monitors per-arena utilization and migrates cold allocations to allow slab reclamation, plus a light-weight background KV sweep that clears tombstones more aggressively when fragmentation thresholds are crossed. Added per-shard fencing to avoid races during concurrent sweep/evict operations.
testing_summary: Unit tests for slab rebalancer invariants and KV sweep fencing added. Integration load tests replaying customer traffic shape show peak GPU memory reduced by ~20-25% and elimination of the reproduced OOMs across 48-hour runs. Canary in staging ran for 72 hours without incident. Performance regression tests confirm p50/p95 latency within 0-1% of baseline.
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Canary): runtime-2.4.1 deployed to 1% of Hosted traffic and 2 non-critical Dedicated nodes for 72h monitoring.
Step 2 (Expanded Canary): If stable, increase to 10% Hosted and 10 Dedicated nodes for 48h.
Step 3 (Dedicated Pilot): Offer to affected customers to schedule Dedicated node upgrade during maintenance window; monitor telemetry for 7 days.
Step 4 (GA): Full roll to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with release notes and migration guide; automated enablement flag defaulted on for Hosted.
Observability: Add slab-utilization and kvcache-tombstone dashboards to console runtime-alloc panel; alert thresholds tuned pre-rollout.
rollback_plan: Rollback to runtime-2.4.0 build if canary shows >1% error rate increase or OOM regression; because the change touches allocator behavior, rollback also triggers a soft warmup to repopulate caches and avoid transient pressure.

notes: This ticket intentionally splits logic between allocator rebalancer (low-level heap) and KV subsystem to minimize blast radius. Feature gated by runtime flag runtime.enable_adaptive_rebalance for staged rollout. Coordinate with Private deployments team for offline upgrade packages.
